function: PPO-based DRL learns the RIS phase shift vectors jointly with offloading destinations to maximize sum offloading efficiency; offloading ratio and computation resources by Dinkelbach (p. 1, 6).
system: Scalar vehicle-RIS-RSU channels (single antenna implied), 2 RSUs, 2-8 passive reflecting RISs (UPA, 30-80 elements, single/double reflection), NOMA uplink, 10 MHz; carrier not stated (p. 3-4, 9, 11).
method: PPO actor-critic DRL (two fully connected networks, 2x128 hidden layers); hybrid action made continuous; J candidate actions scored by the Dinkelbach sub-solver; reinforcement learning (p. 6-9).
data_channel: Own simulated Rician channels for vehicle-RIS, RIS-RIS and RIS-RSU links (factor 5, -20 dB at 1 m, exponents 2.2-3), Poisson vehicle layout; no dataset (p. 3-4, 9).
test_conditions: Convergence runs with 20 vehicles at 60 km/h, 2 RISs, 50 elements; evaluation sweeps vehicles, speed, coverage gap, elements and RISs; retraining per setting not stated (p. 9-11).
baselines: Non-learned: PODORR-BCD [18], PODORR-DE, PODORR-WOA, ORR (Dinkelbach with random destinations and phases), No scheme (all random). Learned: POD, the proposed DRL without the Dinkelbach step (p. 10).
metrics: Sum offloading efficiency (offloaded bits per unit energy), convergence reward curves, execution latency on CPU (p. 9-12).
complexity: Order O((|M|(|K|+1))^3 log(1/e)) with actor inference O(|M|+|S|N); measured CPU latency 0.078-0.095 s versus 8.85-433.20 s for BCD, DE and WOA (p. 8-9, 12).
q1_support: p. 3: "We consider the Rician fading for all three kinds of channels" with hand-set path-loss exponents and Rician factor (p. 9): custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "SOE achieved by various algorithms with different number of" vehicles, speeds, gaps, elements and RISs: parameter sweeps in one simulator; no trained policy is said to be tested on unseen settings, and retraining per setting is not stated.
q3_support: p. 10: "but without adopting Algorithm 2" describes POD, the only DRL benchmark, which is the proposed DRL without the Dinkelbach step (an ablation); BCD, DE, WOA and random schemes are non-learned, so no earlier learned baseline exists.
q4_support: p. 8: "In this section, we analyze the complexity of our proposed" algorithm, giving O((|M|(|K|+1))^3 log(1/e)); p. 12: "EXECUTION LATENCY UNDER DIFFERENT ALGORITHMS" (Table III, read from the page image) lists measured CPU latency.
q5_support: p. 9: "simulation results are presented to verify the" algorithm, using own simulated channels with parameters in Tables I and II; no code or data link, DOI or public dataset is given.
notes: Included, area 3.
